solution:
For x≥0, |x|=x, so the integrand is identically zero. Hence Ip,q=0 whenever p≥0. Taking p=0,q=1 disproves statement 1, which wrongly requires p>0.

For statement 2 take f(x)=1−x. Its derivative is−1 everywhere. If x<0, then f(|x|)=1+x, and the integrand is (1−x)2−(1+x)2=−4x>0. Thus the integral is positive for every p<q<0, contrary to the proposed negative conclusion.

For statement 3, a positive integral cannot have p≥0, since the integrand would be zero on its entire interval. Therefore Ip,q>0 implies p<0. Statement 3 only: answer D.
knowledgePattern: Test only-if claims by splitting a modulus input and choosing a decreasing polynomial
